liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Franklin's Tower** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls this Franklin's Tower the one standout, and says it sounds really different; Reviewer rates this Franklin's Tower alongside the Cornell Morning Dew [10][11][12]
- **Stella Blue** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Stella Blue as a highlight; Reviewer praises excellent Garcia licks in Stella Blue [8][14]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer finds Let It Grow intense, with Garcia playing wildly [12]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Reviewer singles out He's Gone as a highlight [8]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-09-29.sbd.cantor.gmb.96027.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 173 min; rated 3.67/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the sound excellent and the playing delicate and mellow, after listening only to the second set [15]
- **gd1977-09-29.142840.akg.d224e.boswell.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 19 songs; 168 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd77-09-29.sbd.cotsman.9003.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 162 min; rated 4/5 by 15 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the soundboard sound quality as nice [9]
- **gd1977-09-29.142839.akg.d224e.boswell.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 168 min [3]

## Around the show

- Garcia, in a backstage tape dated 10-2-77, recalled this second Seattle night as a really good show [6]
- Garcia, in an interview before the next show in Portland, said the band had unusually rare fun at this show [11]
- Reviewer notes a laid-back, slow show and cannot hear any piano from Keith [17]
- Reviewer finds this second Seattle night better than the previous show [9]
- Reviewer says it falls short of the 10/16/77 show but is still good [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-09-29.sbd.cantor.gmb.96027.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Bill Koucky; source: Betty Cantor 7" two track reel w/DBX-1 @ 7 1/2 ips> PCM501ES @ 44.055 kHz PCM501ES analog out > DBX-1 decoder> analog in PCM501ES analog out>Dat @ 48 kHz First… [1]. Also: Source tape has many pops and hums; first reel lacks DBX, with decoded reels taking over in Sugaree; El Paso is only partial in this source, beginning in its last verse; Edits include removal of squeezed tape start, gain raised in the opening, and a reel change cut in Sugaree [1]
- **gd1977-09-29.142840.akg.d224e.boswell.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Will Boswell; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Matt Smith; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Master Audience Cassettes; AKG D224E mics > Will Boswell's 1st generation reels @ 3 3/4 ips; Transfer Info: 1st generation reels… [2]. Also: Described as the first audience source of this show in general circulation, in July 2018 [2]
- **gd77-09-29.sbd.cotsman.9003.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]. Also: This soundboard copy lacks El Paso [9]
- **gd1977-09-29.142839.akg.d224e.boswell.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Will Boswell; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Matt Smith; source: Source Info: Master Audience Cassettes; AKG D224E mics > Will Boswell's 1st generation reels @ 3 3/4 ips; Transfer Info: 1st generation reels ((Technics… [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by George Alper Grateful Dead: [1977-10-01 Paramount Theater, Portland, OR, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1977-10-01-paramount-theater-portland-or-usa/) [19]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1977-09-29 Thu Paramount Northwest Theatre, Seattle, WA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1411350107970/grateful-dead-1977-09-29-thu-paramount) [20]
